## Broadcasting and journalism career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Broadcasting and journalism career")]

Clooney had an eight-year stint (1958–1966) at [WKYT-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WKYT-TV "WKYT-TV") in [Lexington, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-carmack-5) then went to Ohio to host his own TV show, _The Nick Clooney Show_, first in [Columbus, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio"), for [WLWC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCMH-TV "WCMH-TV") television in 1968, then for [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati")'s [WCPO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCPO-TV "WCPO-TV") in 1969, and finally with its greatest degree of success for crosstown rival [WKRC-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WKRC-TV "WKRC-TV") through the early 1970s. _The Nick Clooney Show_ was a local morning show, with a variety and talk-show format. In December 1974, he gained his first national fame by hosting the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") daytime [game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_show "Game show")_[The Money Maze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Money\_Maze "The Money Maze")_. Broadcast nationally on ABC at 4 p.m., WKRC-TV (at the time an ABC affiliate) delayed _The Money Maze_ so it could be seen back-to-back with _The Nick Clooney Show_ at 10:30 and 11 a.m., respectively.

After ABC canceled _The Money Maze_ on July 4, 1975,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-maze-6) Clooney returned to WKRC-TV and became the station's news director and lead anchor. As a journalist, he is probably best remembered for his coverage of the 1977 [Beverly Hills Supper Club fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Supper_Club_fire "Beverly Hills Supper Club fire") and its aftermath, which spanned several years. Many people in the region first heard about the fire from Clooney when WKRC interrupted its Saturday night prime-time schedule to broadcast news of the fire. Clooney pursued a [hard news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infotainment#Hard_news.2C_soft_news.2C_and_infotainment "Infotainment") focus that was quite different from the [sensationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensationalism "Sensationalism") often seen on local television. Under his leadership, WKRC-TV became a solid #1 in the local news ratings, dethroning CBS affiliate WCPO-TV, which had controlled ratings for more than two decades under [Al Schottelkotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Schottelkotte "Al Schottelkotte")'s leadership.

After leaving WKRC in 1984, Clooney then worked in [Los Angeles, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California"), as the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. co-anchor at [KNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNBC "KNBC"). He returned again to WKRC-TV in the late 1980s, but by that time, [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") affiliate [WLWT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WLWT "WLWT") was number one in the late newscast, with former Cincinnati mayor [Jerry Springer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Springer "Jerry Springer") as its main anchor; Clooney was not able to lead WKRC back to ratings leadership it enjoyed in the past. He moved on to [Salt Lake City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City,_Utah "Salt Lake City, Utah") for several years to anchor and help launch the news operation of the market's [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") station [KSTU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSTU "KSTU") with its 9 p.m. newscast. Then in 1994, Clooney worked a short stint as a news anchor for NBC affiliate [WGRZ-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGRZ-TV "WGRZ-TV") in [Buffalo, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-7) He resurfaced nationally in television as a host and researcher for the [cable channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_channel "Cable channel")[American Movie Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_network) "AMC (TV network)"), where he introduced and presented backgrounds of classic movies, along with [Bob Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)"). In 1999, he returned to his former radio home [WSAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSAI "WSAI") in Cincinnati, starting as afternoon host September 13, then moving to mornings in November to replace [Bob Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Braun "Bob Braun"), who had health problems.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-8)

Because of his long association with WKRC-TV and helping it become one of the dominant stations in the Cincinnati area alongside WCPO-TV, Clooney has been critical of WKRC-TV's current owners, the [Sinclair Broadcast Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group "Sinclair Broadcast Group"), over their [conservative viewpoints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") and their requiring affiliates to run certain news segments known as [must-runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group#Must-run_segments "Sinclair Broadcast Group") during its stations' local newscasts including WKRC-TV. Clooney was critical of Sinclair's mandated commentary scripts known as [journalistic responsibility promos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group#2018_journalistic_responsibility_promos "Sinclair Broadcast Group") during the [first presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump") of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), stating that he would have "quit and become a cab driver" if station management had forced him into reading it on the air.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-9)

## 2004 Congressional campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2004 Congressional campaign")]

Main article: [United States House of Representatives elections, 2004 §Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections,_2004#Kentucky "United States House of Representatives elections, 2004")

Clooney ran as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party "United States Democratic Party") in the [2004 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_election,_2004 "U.S. House election, 2004") for a seat in the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") representing [Kentucky's 4th Congressional District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_4th_congressional_district "Kentucky's 4th congressional district"). His opponent for the [open seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_seat "Open seat") was [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Republican_Party "United States Republican Party")[Geoff Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Davis "Geoff Davis"). Clooney was recruited to run by [Ken Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Lucas_(politician) "Ken Lucas (politician)"), the outgoing Democratic congressman who had held onto the conservative district with his moderate views. With his name recognition and well-publicized endorsement from Lucas, Clooney was a big favorite to keep the seat in Democratic hands.

Early in 2004, Davis fought through a (sometimes rough) three-way Republican [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary "Partisan primary"). The national media began to report on the electoral contest (due to Clooney's famous son [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney")), and Davis began using the phrase "Hollywood vs [the Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_(United_States) "Heartland (United States)")" to describe the race.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-Enquirer2004-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-Telegraph2004-11) Clooney's commanding early lead began to disappear and he was dealt a blow when both _[The Kentucky Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kentucky\_Enquirer "The Kentucky Enquirer")_ and the _Community Press_ newspapers endorsed Davis.

Clooney lost 44% to 54%. During his concession speech, he said his short career in politics was over. He went back to writing a column for _[The Cincinnati Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cincinnati\_Post "The Cincinnati Post")_ three times a week, covering a wide range of topics, until the _Post'_ s discontinuation at the end of 2007.

## Post-Congressional run

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Post-Congressional run")]

In 2006, Clooney and his son George traveled to [Darfur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darfur "Darfur"), [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), and filmed a documentary, _A Journey to Darfur_, which was broadcast on American [cable TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_TV "Cable TV") as well as in [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and France. In 2008, it was released on DVD with the proceeds from its sale being donated to the [International Rescue Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Rescue_Committee "International Rescue Committee") to help the people of Darfur.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-variety-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-time-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-15)

Clooney became an activist for Darfur. He has done several open forums and speeches at local high schools in Ohio and Kentucky, and has participated in different rallies for Darfur. On March 16, 2007, following a Darfur rally, Clooney was awarded an honorary Class of 1952 diploma from [St. Xavier High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier_High_School_(Cincinnati) "St. Xavier High School (Cincinnati)"), the high school he attended in Cincinnati before moving to California.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-St._Xavier_diploma-16) On October 11, 2007, Clooney visited [Turpin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turpin_High_School_(Hamilton_County,_Ohio) "Turpin High School (Hamilton County, Ohio)") in Cincinnati to talk to students about Darfur. The [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky") announced that it would present him with an honorary degree at its 2007 [commencement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduation "Graduation").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-UK-17)

Clooney served as the host of the [Dayton Literary Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton_Literary_Peace_Prize "Dayton Literary Peace Prize") awards ceremony in both 2007[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-2007prize-18) and 2008.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-prize-19)

In fall 2008, Clooney joined the faculty at [American University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University "American University") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") as American University School of Communication and Newseum Distinguished Journalist in Residence. Clooney's appointment is part of a long-term partnership between the School of Communication and the Newseum, the interactive museum of news in Washington, D.C. As part of the school-Newseum partnership, Clooney hosted the fifth annual AU School of Communication-Newseum Reel Journalism Film Festival and other events at the Newseum. "After a news career that stretches back to the Eisenhower administration, I'm looking forward to joining American University's School of Communication and the Newseum to work with a new generation of prospective journalists," said Clooney.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-AU-20)

Clooney taught Opinion Writing in fall 2008, and in spring 2009, he taught Films that Changed Us, a new course based on his book, _The Movies That Changed Us: Reflections on the Screen_ (Atria, 2002). The book analyzes the significance of such iconic American films as _[The Birth of a Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Birth\_of\_a\_Nation "The Birth of a Nation")_, _[The Jazz Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jazz\_Singer "The Jazz Singer")_, _[Dr. Strangelove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr.\_Strangelove "Dr. Strangelove")_, _[Stagecoach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach\_(1939\_film) "Stagecoach (1939 film)")_, _[The Graduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Graduate "The Graduate")_, _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars (film)")_ and _[Saving Private Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving\_Private\_Ryan "Saving Private Ryan")_.

Clooney was the commencement speaker for the [University of Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cincinnati "University of Cincinnati") on June 8, 2012, and was awarded an honorary degree the following day.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-NewsRecord-21)

In 2014, Clooney appeared in _[The Monuments Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monuments\_Men "The Monuments Men")_ which was directed by his son, George Clooney, who played one of the leading characters, Stokes. Nick Clooney played the older Stokes visiting Bruges, Belgium, years later to see the [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_of_Bruges "Madonna of Bruges"), which was one of the many treasures rescued by the Monuments Men.

In 2021, Clooney joined the [Sons of the American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons_of_the_American_Revolution "Sons of the American Revolution").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-NSSAR-22)

**Nicholas Joseph Clooney** (born January 13, 1934) is an American journalist, anchorman, politician, and television host. He is the brother of singers [Rosemary Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Clooney "Rosemary Clooney") and [Betty Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Clooney "Betty Clooney"), also the father of actor [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney") and the uncle of actor [Miguel Ferrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Ferrer "Miguel Ferrer").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Nick%2C_Rosemary_and_Gail_Clooney_1957.JPG/250px-Nick%2C_Rosemary_and_Gail_Clooney_1957.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nick,_Rosemary_and_Gail_Clooney_1957.JPG)

Nick and sisters Rosemary Clooney and Gail Stone at Rosemary's television program, _The Lux Show_, in 1957. Gail did not pursue a career in entertainment.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-obit-1)

Clooney was born in [Maysville, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maysville,_Kentucky "Maysville, Kentucky"), the son of Marie Frances (née Guilfoyle; 1904–1972) and Andrew Joseph Clooney (1902–1974). He was one of five children.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-obit-1) His father was of Irish and German descent and his mother was of Irish ancestry.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-genealogy-2)

While serving as a corporal in the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"),[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] Clooney worked as a [disc jockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disc_jockey "Disc jockey") in the [American Forces Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Forces_Network "American Forces Network") in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), hosting the shows _Music in the Air_ and _Melody-Go-Round_. He then moved to [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") for a try at show business. When that did not work out, Clooney moved to [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"), where he met Nina Warren when she was a contestant in a [beauty pageant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_pageant "Beauty pageant") he was judging; they married in August 1959. In addition to his son, George, Nick Clooney had a daughter named Adelia (known as Ada) (1960–2025).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-3)

## Broadcasting and journalism career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Broadcasting and journalism career")]

Clooney had an eight-year stint (1958–1966) at [WKYT-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WKYT-TV "WKYT-TV") in [Lexington, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-carmack-5) then went to Ohio to host his own TV show, _The Nick Clooney Show_, first in [Columbus, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio"), for [WLWC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCMH-TV "WCMH-TV") television in 1968, then for [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati")'s [WCPO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCPO-TV "WCPO-TV") in 1969, and finally with its greatest degree of success for crosstown rival [WKRC-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WKRC-TV "WKRC-TV") through the early 1970s. _The Nick Clooney Show_ was a local morning show, with a variety and talk-show format. In December 1974, he gained his first national fame by hosting the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") daytime [game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_show "Game show")_[The Money Maze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Money\_Maze "The Money Maze")_. Broadcast nationally on ABC at 4 p.m., WKRC-TV (at the time an ABC affiliate) delayed _The Money Maze_ so it could be seen back-to-back with _The Nick Clooney Show_ at 10:30 and 11 a.m., respectively.

After ABC canceled _The Money Maze_ on July 4, 1975,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-maze-6) Clooney returned to WKRC-TV and became the station's news director and lead anchor. As a journalist, he is probably best remembered for his coverage of the 1977 [Beverly Hills Supper Club fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills_Supper_Club_fire "Beverly Hills Supper Club fire") and its aftermath, which spanned several years. Many people in the region first heard about the fire from Clooney when WKRC interrupted its Saturday night prime-time schedule to broadcast news of the fire. Clooney pursued a [hard news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infotainment#Hard_news.2C_soft_news.2C_and_infotainment "Infotainment") focus that was quite different from the [sensationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensationalism "Sensationalism") often seen on local television. Under his leadership, WKRC-TV became a solid #1 in the local news ratings, dethroning CBS affiliate WCPO-TV, which had controlled ratings for more than two decades under [Al Schottelkotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Schottelkotte "Al Schottelkotte")'s leadership.

After leaving WKRC in 1984, Clooney then worked in [Los Angeles, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California"), as the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. co-anchor at [KNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNBC "KNBC"). He returned again to WKRC-TV in the late 1980s, but by that time, [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") affiliate [WLWT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WLWT "WLWT") was number one in the late newscast, with former Cincinnati mayor [Jerry Springer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Springer "Jerry Springer") as its main anchor; Clooney was not able to lead WKRC back to ratings leadership it enjoyed in the past. He moved on to [Salt Lake City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City,_Utah "Salt Lake City, Utah") for several years to anchor and help launch the news operation of the market's [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") station [KSTU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSTU "KSTU") with its 9 p.m. newscast. Then in 1994, Clooney worked a short stint as a news anchor for NBC affiliate [WGRZ-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGRZ-TV "WGRZ-TV") in [Buffalo, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-7) He resurfaced nationally in television as a host and researcher for the [cable channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_channel "Cable channel")[American Movie Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_network) "AMC (TV network)"), where he introduced and presented backgrounds of classic movies, along with [Bob Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel) "AMC (TV channel)"). In 1999, he returned to his former radio home [WSAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSAI "WSAI") in Cincinnati, starting as afternoon host September 13, then moving to mornings in November to replace [Bob Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Braun "Bob Braun"), who had health problems.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-8)

Because of his long association with WKRC-TV and helping it become one of the dominant stations in the Cincinnati area alongside WCPO-TV, Clooney has been critical of WKRC-TV's current owners, the [Sinclair Broadcast Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group "Sinclair Broadcast Group"), over their [conservative viewpoints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") and their requiring affiliates to run certain news segments known as [must-runs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group#Must-run_segments "Sinclair Broadcast Group") during its stations' local newscasts including WKRC-TV. Clooney was critical of Sinclair's mandated commentary scripts known as [journalistic responsibility promos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinclair_Broadcast_Group#2018_journalistic_responsibility_promos "Sinclair Broadcast Group") during the [first presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump") of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), stating that he would have "quit and become a cab driver" if station management had forced him into reading it on the air.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-9)

## 2004 Congressional campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2004 Congressional campaign")]

Main article: [United States House of Representatives elections, 2004 §Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections,_2004#Kentucky "United States House of Representatives elections, 2004")

Clooney ran as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party "United States Democratic Party") in the [2004 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_election,_2004 "U.S. House election, 2004") for a seat in the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") representing [Kentucky's 4th Congressional District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky's_4th_congressional_district "Kentucky's 4th congressional district"). His opponent for the [open seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_seat "Open seat") was [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Republican_Party "United States Republican Party")[Geoff Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Davis "Geoff Davis"). Clooney was recruited to run by [Ken Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Lucas_(politician) "Ken Lucas (politician)"), the outgoing Democratic congressman who had held onto the conservative district with his moderate views. With his name recognition and well-publicized endorsement from Lucas, Clooney was a big favorite to keep the seat in Democratic hands.

Early in 2004, Davis fought through a (sometimes rough) three-way Republican [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary "Partisan primary"). The national media began to report on the electoral contest (due to Clooney's famous son [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney")), and Davis began using the phrase "Hollywood vs [the Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_(United_States) "Heartland (United States)")" to describe the race.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-Enquirer2004-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-Telegraph2004-11) Clooney's commanding early lead began to disappear and he was dealt a blow when both _[The Kentucky Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kentucky\_Enquirer "The Kentucky Enquirer")_ and the _Community Press_ newspapers endorsed Davis.

Clooney lost 44% to 54%. During his concession speech, he said his short career in politics was over. He went back to writing a column for _[The Cincinnati Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cincinnati\_Post "The Cincinnati Post")_ three times a week, covering a wide range of topics, until the _Post'_ s discontinuation at the end of 2007.

## Post-Congressional run

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nick_Clooney&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Post-Congressional run")]

In 2006, Clooney and his son George traveled to [Darfur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darfur "Darfur"), [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), and filmed a documentary, _A Journey to Darfur_, which was broadcast on American [cable TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_TV "Cable TV") as well as in [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and France. In 2008, it was released on DVD with the proceeds from its sale being donated to the [International Rescue Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Rescue_Committee "International Rescue Committee") to help the people of Darfur.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-variety-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-time-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-15)

Clooney became an activist for Darfur. He has done several open forums and speeches at local high schools in Ohio and Kentucky, and has participated in different rallies for Darfur. On March 16, 2007, following a Darfur rally, Clooney was awarded an honorary Class of 1952 diploma from [St. Xavier High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier_High_School_(Cincinnati) "St. Xavier High School (Cincinnati)"), the high school he attended in Cincinnati before moving to California.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-St._Xavier_diploma-16) On October 11, 2007, Clooney visited [Turpin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turpin_High_School_(Hamilton_County,_Ohio) "Turpin High School (Hamilton County, Ohio)") in Cincinnati to talk to students about Darfur. The [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky") announced that it would present him with an honorary degree at its 2007 [commencement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduation "Graduation").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-UK-17)

Clooney served as the host of the [Dayton Literary Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton_Literary_Peace_Prize "Dayton Literary Peace Prize") awards ceremony in both 2007[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-2007prize-18) and 2008.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-prize-19)

In fall 2008, Clooney joined the faculty at [American University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University "American University") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") as American University School of Communication and Newseum Distinguished Journalist in Residence. Clooney's appointment is part of a long-term partnership between the School of Communication and the Newseum, the interactive museum of news in Washington, D.C. As part of the school-Newseum partnership, Clooney hosted the fifth annual AU School of Communication-Newseum Reel Journalism Film Festival and other events at the Newseum. "After a news career that stretches back to the Eisenhower administration, I'm looking forward to joining American University's School of Communication and the Newseum to work with a new generation of prospective journalists," said Clooney.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-AU-20)

Clooney taught Opinion Writing in fall 2008, and in spring 2009, he taught Films that Changed Us, a new course based on his book, _The Movies That Changed Us: Reflections on the Screen_ (Atria, 2002). The book analyzes the significance of such iconic American films as _[The Birth of a Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Birth\_of\_a\_Nation "The Birth of a Nation")_, _[The Jazz Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jazz\_Singer "The Jazz Singer")_, _[Dr. Strangelove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr.\_Strangelove "Dr. Strangelove")_, _[Stagecoach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach\_(1939\_film) "Stagecoach (1939 film)")_, _[The Graduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Graduate "The Graduate")_, _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars (film)")_ and _[Saving Private Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving\_Private\_Ryan "Saving Private Ryan")_.

Clooney was the commencement speaker for the [University of Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cincinnati "University of Cincinnati") on June 8, 2012, and was awarded an honorary degree the following day.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-NewsRecord-21)

In 2014, Clooney appeared in _[The Monuments Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Monuments\_Men "The Monuments Men")_ which was directed by his son, George Clooney, who played one of the leading characters, Stokes. Nick Clooney played the older Stokes visiting Bruges, Belgium, years later to see the [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_of_Bruges "Madonna of Bruges"), which was one of the many treasures rescued by the Monuments Men.

In 2021, Clooney joined the [Sons of the American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons_of_the_American_Revolution "Sons of the American Revolution").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Clooney#cite_note-NSSAR-22)

English film and theatre director (1926–2003)

This article is about the director. For the attorney, see [Marilyn Milian §Personal life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Milian#Personal_life "Marilyn Milian").

**John Richard Schlesinger**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-ODNB-1) ([/ˈ ʃ l ɛ s ɪ n dʒ ər/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_SHLESS-in-jər_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); 16 February 1926 – 25 July 2003) was an English film, television and theatre director, and actor. He emerged in the early 1960s as a leading light of the [British New Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_New_Wave "British New Wave"), before embarking on a successful career in [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States"), often directing films dealing with provocative subject matter, combined with his status as one of the rare openly gay directors working in mainstream films.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-Breznica-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-3)

Schlesinger started his career making British [kitchen sink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_sink_realism "Kitchen sink realism") dramas _[A Kind of Loving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Kind\_of\_Loving\_(film) "A Kind of Loving (film)")_ (1962) and [_Billy Liar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Liar_(film) "Billy Liar (film)") (1963), and the [Thomas Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hardy "Thomas Hardy") adaptation [_Far from the Madding Crowd_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_from_the_Madding_Crowd_(1967_film) "Far from the Madding Crowd (1967 film)") (1967). He won the [Academy Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") for _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_ (1969) and was Oscar-nominated for _[Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darling\_(1965\_film) "Darling (1965 film)")_ (1965) and [_Sunday Bloody Sunday_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_Bloody_Sunday_(film) "Sunday Bloody Sunday (film)") (1971). He gained acclaim for his [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") films _[The Day of the Locust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Day\_of\_the\_Locust\_(film) "The Day of the Locust (film)")_ (1975) and _[Marathon Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon\_Man\_(film) "Marathon Man (film)")_ (1976). His later films include _[Madame Sousatzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame\_Sousatzka "Madame Sousatzka")_ (1988) and _[Cold Comfort Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Comfort\_Farm\_(film) "Cold Comfort Farm (film)")_ (1995). He also served as an associate director of the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre").

Over his career he received numerous accolades including an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), four [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs"), and a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe "Golden Globe"). His honours include the [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Commander of the Order of the British Empire") (CBE), and a [BAFTA Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Fellow "BAFTA Fellow"). Four of Schlesinger's films are on the [British Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute "British Film Institute")'s [Top 100 British films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFI_Top_100_British_films "BFI Top 100 British films").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-4)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early years and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years and education")]

Schlesinger was born and raised in [Hampstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampstead "Hampstead"), London,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-5) in a Jewish family,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-6) the eldest of five children[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-7) of distinguished [Emmanuel College, Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_College,_Cambridge "Emmanuel College, Cambridge")–educated paediatrician and physician Bernard Edward Schlesinger [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Order of the British Empire")[FRCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Royal_College_of_Physicians "Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians") (1896–1984), who had also served in the [Royal Army Medical Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Army_Medical_Corps "Royal Army Medical Corps") as a brigadier,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-8) and his wife Winifred Henrietta, daughter of Hermann Regensburg, a stockbroker from [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-9) She had left school at 14 to study at the [Trinity College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_College_of_Music "Trinity College of Music"), and later studied languages at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") for three years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-11) Bernard Schlesinger's father Richard, a stockbroker, had come to England in the 1880s from Frankfurt.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-12)

After [St Edmund's School, Hindhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Edmund's_School,_Hindhead "St Edmund's School, Hindhead") and [Uppingham School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uppingham_School "Uppingham School") (where his father had also been),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-13) Schlesinger enlisted in the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). While serving with the [Royal Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Engineers "Royal Engineers"), he made films on the war's front line. He also entertained his fellow troops by performing magic tricks.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-14) After his tour of duty, he continued making short films and acted in stage productions while studying at [Balliol College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balliol_College "Balliol College"), [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford"), where he was involved in the [Oxford University Dramatic Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Dramatic_Society "Oxford University Dramatic Society").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-bl-15)

### Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

Schlesinger's acting career began in the 1950s and consisted of supporting roles in British films such as _[The Divided Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Divided\_Heart "The Divided Heart")_ and _[Oh... Rosalinda!!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh...\_Rosalinda!! "Oh... Rosalinda!!")_, and British television productions such as _[BBC Sunday Night Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Theatre "BBC Sunday Night Theatre")_, _[The Adventures of Robin Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Robin\_Hood\_(TV\_series) "The Adventures of Robin Hood (TV series)")_ and _The Vise_. He began his directorial career in 1956 with the short documentary _Sunday in the Park_ about London's [Hyde Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London "Hyde Park, London"). In 1958, Schlesinger created a documentary on [Benjamin Britten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Britten "Benjamin Britten") and the [Aldeburgh Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldeburgh_Festival "Aldeburgh Festival") for the BBC's _[Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monitor\_(UK\_TV\_series) "Monitor (UK TV series)")_ TV programme, including rehearsals of the children's opera _[Noye's Fludde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noye's\_Fludde "Noye's Fludde")_ featuring a young [Michael Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Crawford "Michael Crawford").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-17) In 1959, Schlesinger was credited as exterior or second unit director on 23 episodes of the TV series _[The Four Just Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Just\_Men\_(TV\_series) "The Four Just Men (TV series)")_ and four 30-minute episodes of the series _[Danger Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danger\_Man "Danger Man")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-18) He also appeared in _Col March of Scotland Yard_ as "Dutch cook" in "Death and the Other Monkey" 1956.

By the 1960s, he had virtually given up acting to concentrate on a directing career, and another of his earlier directorial efforts, the [British Transport Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Transport_Films "British Transport Films")' documentary _[Terminus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminus\_(1961\_film) "Terminus (1961 film)")_ (1961), gained a [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival") Gold Lion and a [British Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Award "British Academy Award"). His first two fiction films, _[A Kind of Loving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Kind\_of\_Loving\_(film) "A Kind of Loving (film)")_ (1962) and _[Billy Liar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Liar\_(film) "Billy Liar (film)")_ (1963) were set in the [North of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_of_England "North of England"). Both were produced by Joseph Janni and financed by [Nat Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nat_Cohen "Nat Cohen").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-three-19)_A Kind of Loving_ won the [Golden Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear "Golden Bear") award at the [12th Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_Berlin_International_Film_Festival "12th Berlin International Film Festival") in 1962.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-berlinale_1962-20) His third feature film, _[Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darling\_(1965\_film) "Darling (1965 film)")_ (1965), tartly described the modern way of life in London and was one of the first films about '[swinging London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swinging_London "Swinging London")'. Schlesinger's next film was the period drama _[Far from the Madding Crowd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far\_from\_the\_Madding\_Crowd\_(1967\_film) "Far from the Madding Crowd (1967 film)")_ (1967), an adaptation of [Thomas Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hardy "Thomas Hardy")'s popular novel accentuated by beautiful English country locations. Both films (and _Billy Liar_) featured [Julie Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Christie "Julie Christie") as the female lead.

Schlesinger's next film, _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_ (1969), was internationally acclaimed. A story of two hustlers living on the fringe in the bad side of New York City, it was Schlesinger's first film shot in the US, and it won [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscars "Oscars") for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Directing "Academy Award for Directing") and [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). The film was one of the earliest mainstream American films to deal explicitly with homosexual relationships, and is considered a groundbreaking work of queer cinema.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-23) However, according to actor [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), at a preview screening of the film "people walked out in droves" after seeing a male student go down on the male main character in a Times Square [grindhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grindhouse "Grindhouse"). "We thought this could end everybody's career," said Hoffman.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-24)

During the 1970s, Schlesinger made an array of films that were mainly about loners, losers and people outside the mainstream world, such as _[Sunday Bloody Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday\_Bloody\_Sunday\_(film) "Sunday Bloody Sunday (film)")_ (1971), _[The Day of the Locust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Day\_of\_the\_Locust\_(film) "The Day of the Locust (film)")_ (1975), _[Marathon Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon\_Man\_(film) "Marathon Man (film)")_ (1976) and _[Yanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanks "Yanks")_ (1979). Later, came the major box office and critical failure of _[Honky Tonk Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky\_Tonk\_Freeway "Honky Tonk Freeway")_ (1981), followed by films that attracted mixed responses from the public, and low returns, although _[The Falcon and the Snowman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Falcon\_and\_the\_Snowman "The Falcon and the Snowman")_ (1985) made money and _[Pacific Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific\_Heights\_(film) "Pacific Heights (film)")_ (1990) was a box-office hit. In Britain, he did better with films like _[Madame Sousatzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame\_Sousatzka "Madame Sousatzka")_ (1988) and the television film _[Cold Comfort Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Comfort\_Farm\_(film) "Cold Comfort Farm (film)")_ (1995). Other later works include plays for television _[An Englishman Abroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Englishman\_Abroad "An Englishman Abroad")_ (1983) and _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1991), both with scripts by Alan Bennett, _[The Innocent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Innocent\_(1993\_film) "The Innocent (1993 film)")_ (1993) and _[The Next Best Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Next\_Best\_Thing "The Next Best Thing")_ (2000).

Schlesinger directed on stage _Timon of Athens_ (1965) for the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") and the musical _[I and Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_and\_Albert "I and Albert")_ (1972) at London's [Piccadilly Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piccadilly_Theatre "Piccadilly Theatre"). From 1973, he was an associate director of the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre"), where he produced [George Bernard Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Bernard_Shaw "George Bernard Shaw")'s _[Heartbreak House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartbreak\_House "Heartbreak House")_ (1975). He directed several operas, including _[Les contes d'Hoffmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les\_contes\_d'Hoffmann "Les contes d'Hoffmann")_ (1980) and _[Der Rosenkavalier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der\_Rosenkavalier "Der Rosenkavalier")_ (1984), both at [Covent Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covent_Garden "Covent Garden").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-25)

Schlesinger directed _[The Journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Journey\_(party\_political\_broadcast) "The Journey (party political broadcast)")_, a [party political broadcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_political_broadcast "Party political broadcast") for the [Conservative Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") in the [general election of 1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_Kingdom_general_election "1992 United Kingdom general election"), which featured Prime Minister [John Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Major "John Major") returning to [Brixton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brixton "Brixton") in [south London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London"), thus highlighting Major's humble background, something atypical for a Conservative politician at that time.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-SO-26) Schlesinger said he had voted for all three main political parties in the UK at one time or another.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Later years and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Later years and death")]

In 1991, Schlesinger made a brief return to acting, portraying the gay character 'Derek' in the TV adaptation of _[The Lost Language of Cranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_Language\_of\_Cranes\_(film) "The Lost Language of Cranes (film)")_ for the BBC. Schlesinger had himself come out during the making of _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-27)

Schlesinger was appointed [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Commander of the Order of the British Empire") (CBE) in the [1970 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Birthday_Honours#Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire_(CBE) "1970 Birthday Honours") for services to film.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-diaries-29) Maintaining a flat in London and house at [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-30) Schlesinger had a Golden Palm Star on the Palm Springs [Walk of Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs_Walk_of_Stars "Palm Springs Walk of Stars") dedicated to him in January 2003, which was his final public appearance.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-32)

Schlesinger underwent a quadruple [heart bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_bypass "Heart bypass") in 1998, before suffering a [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrovascular_accident "Cerebrovascular accident") on New Year's Day 2001, which substantially diminished his faculties.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-33) He died at Desert Regional Medical Center in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California") on the morning of 25 July 2003, aged 77.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-auto-34)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-Breznica-2)

A memorial service was held on 30 September 2003.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-diaries-29) He was cremated, with most of his ashes interred next to his parents and the remainder left to be interred with Childers.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-auto-34)

## Accolades and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Accolades and honours")]

He was twice nominated for the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival")'s [Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Lion "Golden Lion"), and was recipient of the [Directors Guild of Great Britain's Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_Great_Britain#Lifetime_Achievement_Awards "Directors Guild of Great Britain"). In the [1970 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Birthday_Honours#Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire_(CBE) "1970 Birthday Honours"), he was appointed [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (CBE) for services to film. In 1981, the [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg")-based [Alfred Toepfer Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Toepfer_Foundation "Alfred Toepfer Foundation") awarded Schlesinger its annual [Shakespeare Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare_Prize "Shakespeare Prize") in recognition of his life's work. In [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_British_Academy_Film_Awards#BAFTA_Fellowship "49th British Academy Film Awards") he was made a [BAFTA Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Fellowship "BAFTA Fellowship").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

English film and theatre director (1926–2003)

This article is about the director. For the attorney, see [Marilyn Milian §Personal life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Milian#Personal_life "Marilyn Milian").

**John Richard Schlesinger**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-ODNB-1) ([/ˈ ʃ l ɛ s ɪ n dʒ ər/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_SHLESS-in-jər_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); 16 February 1926 – 25 July 2003) was an English film, television and theatre director, and actor. He emerged in the early 1960s as a leading light of the [British New Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_New_Wave "British New Wave"), before embarking on a successful career in [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States"), often directing films dealing with provocative subject matter, combined with his status as one of the rare openly gay directors working in mainstream films.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-Breznica-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-3)

Schlesinger started his career making British [kitchen sink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_sink_realism "Kitchen sink realism") dramas _[A Kind of Loving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Kind\_of\_Loving\_(film) "A Kind of Loving (film)")_ (1962) and [_Billy Liar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Liar_(film) "Billy Liar (film)") (1963), and the [Thomas Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hardy "Thomas Hardy") adaptation [_Far from the Madding Crowd_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_from_the_Madding_Crowd_(1967_film) "Far from the Madding Crowd (1967 film)") (1967). He won the [Academy Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") for _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_ (1969) and was Oscar-nominated for _[Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darling\_(1965\_film) "Darling (1965 film)")_ (1965) and [_Sunday Bloody Sunday_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_Bloody_Sunday_(film) "Sunday Bloody Sunday (film)") (1971). He gained acclaim for his [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") films _[The Day of the Locust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Day\_of\_the\_Locust\_(film) "The Day of the Locust (film)")_ (1975) and _[Marathon Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon\_Man\_(film) "Marathon Man (film)")_ (1976). His later films include _[Madame Sousatzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame\_Sousatzka "Madame Sousatzka")_ (1988) and _[Cold Comfort Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Comfort\_Farm\_(film) "Cold Comfort Farm (film)")_ (1995). He also served as an associate director of the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre").

Over his career he received numerous accolades including an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), four [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs"), and a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe "Golden Globe"). His honours include the [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Commander of the Order of the British Empire") (CBE), and a [BAFTA Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Fellow "BAFTA Fellow"). Four of Schlesinger's films are on the [British Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Institute "British Film Institute")'s [Top 100 British films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFI_Top_100_British_films "BFI Top 100 British films").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-4)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early years and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years and education")]

Schlesinger was born and raised in [Hampstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampstead "Hampstead"), London,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-5) in a Jewish family,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-6) the eldest of five children[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-7) of distinguished [Emmanuel College, Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_College,_Cambridge "Emmanuel College, Cambridge")–educated paediatrician and physician Bernard Edward Schlesinger [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Order of the British Empire")[FRCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Royal_College_of_Physicians "Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians") (1896–1984), who had also served in the [Royal Army Medical Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Army_Medical_Corps "Royal Army Medical Corps") as a brigadier,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-8) and his wife Winifred Henrietta, daughter of Hermann Regensburg, a stockbroker from [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-9) She had left school at 14 to study at the [Trinity College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_College_of_Music "Trinity College of Music"), and later studied languages at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") for three years.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-11) Bernard Schlesinger's father Richard, a stockbroker, had come to England in the 1880s from Frankfurt.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-12)

After [St Edmund's School, Hindhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Edmund's_School,_Hindhead "St Edmund's School, Hindhead") and [Uppingham School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uppingham_School "Uppingham School") (where his father had also been),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-13) Schlesinger enlisted in the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). While serving with the [Royal Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Engineers "Royal Engineers"), he made films on the war's front line. He also entertained his fellow troops by performing magic tricks.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-14) After his tour of duty, he continued making short films and acted in stage productions while studying at [Balliol College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balliol_College "Balliol College"), [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford"), where he was involved in the [Oxford University Dramatic Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Dramatic_Society "Oxford University Dramatic Society").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-bl-15)

### Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Career")]

Schlesinger's acting career began in the 1950s and consisted of supporting roles in British films such as _[The Divided Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Divided\_Heart "The Divided Heart")_ and _[Oh... Rosalinda!!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh...\_Rosalinda!! "Oh... Rosalinda!!")_, and British television productions such as _[BBC Sunday Night Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Theatre "BBC Sunday Night Theatre")_, _[The Adventures of Robin Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Robin\_Hood\_(TV\_series) "The Adventures of Robin Hood (TV series)")_ and _The Vise_. He began his directorial career in 1956 with the short documentary _Sunday in the Park_ about London's [Hyde Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_London "Hyde Park, London"). In 1958, Schlesinger created a documentary on [Benjamin Britten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Britten "Benjamin Britten") and the [Aldeburgh Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldeburgh_Festival "Aldeburgh Festival") for the BBC's _[Monitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monitor\_(UK\_TV\_series) "Monitor (UK TV series)")_ TV programme, including rehearsals of the children's opera _[Noye's Fludde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noye's\_Fludde "Noye's Fludde")_ featuring a young [Michael Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Crawford "Michael Crawford").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-17) In 1959, Schlesinger was credited as exterior or second unit director on 23 episodes of the TV series _[The Four Just Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Just\_Men\_(TV\_series) "The Four Just Men (TV series)")_ and four 30-minute episodes of the series _[Danger Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danger\_Man "Danger Man")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-18) He also appeared in _Col March of Scotland Yard_ as "Dutch cook" in "Death and the Other Monkey" 1956.

By the 1960s, he had virtually given up acting to concentrate on a directing career, and another of his earlier directorial efforts, the [British Transport Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Transport_Films "British Transport Films")' documentary _[Terminus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminus\_(1961\_film) "Terminus (1961 film)")_ (1961), gained a [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival") Gold Lion and a [British Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Award "British Academy Award"). His first two fiction films, _[A Kind of Loving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Kind\_of\_Loving\_(film) "A Kind of Loving (film)")_ (1962) and _[Billy Liar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Liar\_(film) "Billy Liar (film)")_ (1963) were set in the [North of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_of_England "North of England"). Both were produced by Joseph Janni and financed by [Nat Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nat_Cohen "Nat Cohen").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-three-19)_A Kind of Loving_ won the [Golden Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear "Golden Bear") award at the [12th Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_Berlin_International_Film_Festival "12th Berlin International Film Festival") in 1962.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-berlinale_1962-20) His third feature film, _[Darling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darling\_(1965\_film) "Darling (1965 film)")_ (1965), tartly described the modern way of life in London and was one of the first films about '[swinging London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swinging_London "Swinging London")'. Schlesinger's next film was the period drama _[Far from the Madding Crowd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far\_from\_the\_Madding\_Crowd\_(1967\_film) "Far from the Madding Crowd (1967 film)")_ (1967), an adaptation of [Thomas Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hardy "Thomas Hardy")'s popular novel accentuated by beautiful English country locations. Both films (and _Billy Liar_) featured [Julie Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Christie "Julie Christie") as the female lead.

Schlesinger's next film, _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_ (1969), was internationally acclaimed. A story of two hustlers living on the fringe in the bad side of New York City, it was Schlesinger's first film shot in the US, and it won [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscars "Oscars") for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Directing "Academy Award for Directing") and [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). The film was one of the earliest mainstream American films to deal explicitly with homosexual relationships, and is considered a groundbreaking work of queer cinema.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-23) However, according to actor [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), at a preview screening of the film "people walked out in droves" after seeing a male student go down on the male main character in a Times Square [grindhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grindhouse "Grindhouse"). "We thought this could end everybody's career," said Hoffman.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-24)

During the 1970s, Schlesinger made an array of films that were mainly about loners, losers and people outside the mainstream world, such as _[Sunday Bloody Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday\_Bloody\_Sunday\_(film) "Sunday Bloody Sunday (film)")_ (1971), _[The Day of the Locust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Day\_of\_the\_Locust\_(film) "The Day of the Locust (film)")_ (1975), _[Marathon Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon\_Man\_(film) "Marathon Man (film)")_ (1976) and _[Yanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanks "Yanks")_ (1979). Later, came the major box office and critical failure of _[Honky Tonk Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky\_Tonk\_Freeway "Honky Tonk Freeway")_ (1981), followed by films that attracted mixed responses from the public, and low returns, although _[The Falcon and the Snowman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Falcon\_and\_the\_Snowman "The Falcon and the Snowman")_ (1985) made money and _[Pacific Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific\_Heights\_(film) "Pacific Heights (film)")_ (1990) was a box-office hit. In Britain, he did better with films like _[Madame Sousatzka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame\_Sousatzka "Madame Sousatzka")_ (1988) and the television film _[Cold Comfort Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Comfort\_Farm\_(film) "Cold Comfort Farm (film)")_ (1995). Other later works include plays for television _[An Englishman Abroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Englishman\_Abroad "An Englishman Abroad")_ (1983) and _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1991), both with scripts by Alan Bennett, _[The Innocent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Innocent\_(1993\_film) "The Innocent (1993 film)")_ (1993) and _[The Next Best Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Next\_Best\_Thing "The Next Best Thing")_ (2000).

Schlesinger directed on stage _Timon of Athens_ (1965) for the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") and the musical _[I and Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_and\_Albert "I and Albert")_ (1972) at London's [Piccadilly Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piccadilly_Theatre "Piccadilly Theatre"). From 1973, he was an associate director of the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre"), where he produced [George Bernard Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Bernard_Shaw "George Bernard Shaw")'s _[Heartbreak House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartbreak\_House "Heartbreak House")_ (1975). He directed several operas, including _[Les contes d'Hoffmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les\_contes\_d'Hoffmann "Les contes d'Hoffmann")_ (1980) and _[Der Rosenkavalier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der\_Rosenkavalier "Der Rosenkavalier")_ (1984), both at [Covent Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covent_Garden "Covent Garden").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-25)

Schlesinger directed _[The Journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Journey\_(party\_political\_broadcast) "The Journey (party political broadcast)")_, a [party political broadcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_political_broadcast "Party political broadcast") for the [Conservative Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") in the [general election of 1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_Kingdom_general_election "1992 United Kingdom general election"), which featured Prime Minister [John Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Major "John Major") returning to [Brixton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brixton "Brixton") in [south London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London"), thus highlighting Major's humble background, something atypical for a Conservative politician at that time.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-SO-26) Schlesinger said he had voted for all three main political parties in the UK at one time or another.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Later years and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Later years and death")]

In 1991, Schlesinger made a brief return to acting, portraying the gay character 'Derek' in the TV adaptation of _[The Lost Language of Cranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_Language\_of\_Cranes\_(film) "The Lost Language of Cranes (film)")_ for the BBC. Schlesinger had himself come out during the making of _[Midnight Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Cowboy "Midnight Cowboy")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-27)

Schlesinger was appointed [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Commander of the Order of the British Empire") (CBE) in the [1970 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Birthday_Honours#Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire_(CBE) "1970 Birthday Honours") for services to film.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-diaries-29) Maintaining a flat in London and house at [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-30) Schlesinger had a Golden Palm Star on the Palm Springs [Walk of Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs_Walk_of_Stars "Palm Springs Walk of Stars") dedicated to him in January 2003, which was his final public appearance.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-32)

Schlesinger underwent a quadruple [heart bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_bypass "Heart bypass") in 1998, before suffering a [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrovascular_accident "Cerebrovascular accident") on New Year's Day 2001, which substantially diminished his faculties.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-33) He died at Desert Regional Medical Center in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California") on the morning of 25 July 2003, aged 77.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-auto-34)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-Breznica-2)

A memorial service was held on 30 September 2003.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-diaries-29) He was cremated, with most of his ashes interred next to his parents and the remainder left to be interred with Childers.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Schlesinger#cite_note-auto-34)

## Accolades and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Schlesinger&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Accolades and honours")]

He was twice nominated for the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival")'s [Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Lion "Golden Lion"), and was recipient of the [Directors Guild of Great Britain's Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_Great_Britain#Lifetime_Achievement_Awards "Directors Guild of Great Britain"). In the [1970 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Birthday_Honours#Commander_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire_(CBE) "1970 Birthday Honours"), he was appointed [Commander of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (CBE) for services to film. In 1981, the [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg")-based [Alfred Toepfer Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Toepfer_Foundation "Alfred Toepfer Foundation") awarded Schlesinger its annual [Shakespeare Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare_Prize "Shakespeare Prize") in recognition of his life's work. In [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_British_Academy_Film_Awards#BAFTA_Fellowship "49th British Academy Film Awards") he was made a [BAFTA Fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Fellowship "BAFTA Fellowship").
